newsitem.title: UK: U.K. Intervention Board details EU sugar sales.
newsitem.headline: U.K. Intervention Board details EU sugar sales.

text.p: A total 40,550 tonnes of current series white sugar received export rebates of a maximum 42.889 European Currency Units (Ecus) per 100 kilos at Wednesday's European Union (EU) tender, the U.K. Intervention Board said.
Out of this, traders in France received 20,300 tonnes, in the U.K. 10,000, in Germany 7,000, in Belgium 3,000 and in Spain 250 tonnes, it added.

This week's award brings the cumulative tonnage awarded for export from the 1996/97 crop to 2.290 million tonnes. This compares with the 100,050 tonnes awarded on June 26, 1996, when the cumulative tonnage totalled 2.488 million tonnes.
Earlier on Wednesday, London traders had expected the subsidy for the current season whites campaign for licences to end-September to be 42.889 Ecus per 100 kilos, the exact amount awarded.
Traders had also forecast the total authorised sugar tonnage export awards to be between 25,000 and 40,000 tonnes versus 30,350 last week when the restitution was 42.168 Ecus.
